To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a large outbreak of vomiting occurred in 50 nurseries in South England in May 2012 and that the outbreak was caused by Bacillus cereus toxin produced by the bacteria in food supplied to the nurseries by the same catering company.

• An outbreak of food poisoning occurred in nurseries in south east England in May 2012 • The outbreak was due to Bacillus cereus toxin produced by bacteria growing on beans soaked at room temperature • The outbreak was prevented by improved food preparation and storage • The outbreak was investigated by the local Health Protection Teams, Public Health England and the Food Standards Agency • The findings of the investigation were shared with the food business and the public • The findings were published in the Journal of Public Health

1) A large outbreak of vomiting was reported in nurseries in the South East of England in May 2012 2) Epidemiological and microbiological investigation demonstrated that this outbreak of vomiting in children was caused by the bacterium Bacillus cereus 3) Laboratory investigations showed that conditions used for soaking of navy beans were likely to have caused growth and toxin production in B. cereus, and therefore caused the outbreak of vomiting.

this outbreak was caused by the consumption of food containing Bacillus cereus toxin, most likely produced by B. cereus growing in the food prior to cooking.
the outbreak was caused by the consumption of food prepared by the catering company that had been stored for an excessive period of time at an inappropriate temperature.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the outbreak was caused by Bacillus cereus and the likely source was undercooked haricot beans.
the outbreak of foodborne illness was due to a combination of poor temperature control and poor cooking practices.
the outbreak was caused by the growth and toxin production by B. cereus in soaked haricot beans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
food poisoning can be caused by a range of organisms, including bacteria, parasites and viruses.
it is important to ensure that food is cooked to a high enough temperature to kill any bacteria present.
food safety is everyone's responsibility.
